subject: slingshot spider web
title: This Spider Fires Itself at Prey With 130 Times the Force of Gravity

scenes.text: This spider turns its own web into a slingshot.
It's about a millimeter long and lives in the Amazon rainforest of Peru.
It pulls its web back with its front legs and holds it stretched, sometimes for hours.
When a mosquito flies close, it lets go. Spider and web shoot forward together at four meters a second.
The acceleration is about 130 times gravity. A hundred times a cheetah's.
A fighter pilot blacks out at less than a tenth of that. To set it off, scientists just snapped their fingers.

description:
The slingshot spider launches itself and its web at flying insects.
Georgia Tech researchers working in the Peruvian Amazon measured the launch at about 1,300 metres per second squared, roughly 130 times gravity and 100 times the acceleration of a cheetah, reaching about 4 metres per second. The spider, about a millimetre long, can hold the stretched web ready for hours, and fired when researchers snapped their fingers, which suggests it senses prey by sound. The study appeared in Current Biology in 2020.
Which tiny animal has the biggest superpower?
first_comment: If it misses, it just pulls the line back and reloads. Which tiny animal should we measure next?
